text_blocks.snippet: To manage excruciating arthritis pain, a combination of approaches, including medication, physical therapy, and self-care strategies, can be effective. Over-the-counter and prescription medications like NSAIDs can help reduce pain and inflammation. Additionally, physical therapy, including exercises and manual therapy, can improve joint flexibility and strength. Heat and cold therapy, massage, and assistive devices can also provide relief.
snippet_highlighted_words: medication, physical therapy, and self-care strategies

list.snippet: Over-the-counter (OTC) pain relievers: NSAIDs like ibuprofen and naproxen can help reduce pain and inflammation.
Prescription medications: Stronger pain relievers like opioids may be considered in severe cases, but they carry potential risks and side effects.
Topical medications: Creams and gels containing NSAIDs or other pain-relieving ingredients can be applied directly to the affected area.

list.title: Exercise:
list.snippet: A regular exercise routine, including low-impact activities like walking, swimming, or cycling, can improve joint flexibility, strength, and reduce pain.

list.title: Physical therapy:
list.snippet: A physical therapist can guide you through exercises and stretches tailored to your specific needs, as well as provide manual therapy techniques like massage.

list.title: Heat and cold therapy:
list.snippet: Applying heat can relax muscles and improve blood flow, while cold therapy can reduce swelling and numb pain.

list.title: Weight management:
list.snippet: Losing excess weight can reduce stress on weight-bearing joints.

list.title: Assistive devices:
list.snippet: Canes, walkers, or braces can provide support and reduce stress on affected joints.

list.title: Mind-body techniques:
list.snippet: Relaxation techniques like meditation, deep breathing, and yoga can help manage pain and stress.
Acupuncture: Some individuals find relief from arthritis pain through acupuncture, a traditional Chinese therapy involving the insertion of thin needles at specific points on the body.
Massage: Massage therapy can help improve blood flow and reduce muscle stiffness.
If your arthritis pain is severe or persistent, consult with a healthcare professional for a proper diagnosis and treatment plan.
If you experience any concerning side effects from medications, seek medical advice.
If you're considering complementary therapies, discuss them with your doctor to ensure they are safe and appropriate for your condition.

related_questions.question: What are the 7 types of arthritis?

text_blocks.snippet: There are more than 100 different types of arthritis, but some of the most common include osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, gout, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, juvenile arthritis, and lupus. These conditions all involve joint pain and inflammation, but they differ in their causes, symptoms, and affected areas.
snippet_highlighted_words: osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, gout, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, juvenile arthritis, and lupus

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a brief overview of each:

list.title: Osteoarthritis (OA):
list.snippet: The most common type, OA is caused by the breakdown of cartilage in joints, leading to bone-on-bone friction.

list.title: Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA):
list.snippet: An autoimmune disorder where the body's immune system attacks the lining of the joints.

list.title: Gout:
list.snippet: A metabolic condition caused by a buildup of uric acid crystals in the joints, often affecting the big toe.

list.title: Psoriatic Arthritis (PsA):
list.snippet: An inflammatory arthritis associated with the skin condition psoriasis, affecting joints, skin, and nails.

list.title: Ankylosing Spondylitis:
list.snippet: Primarily affects the spine, causing inflammation and stiffness in the spinal joints.

list.title: Juvenile Arthritis (JA):
list.snippet: A group of inflammatory conditions affecting children and teens, with various subtypes.

list.title: Lupus:
list.snippet: An autoimmune disease that can affect various parts of the body, including the joints, skin, and organs.
